Controls.accumulationEscapeTip: Seconds the ball has to escape before it freezes in place.
Controls.spikesTip: Add inward-pointing spikes on the outer wall as obstacles.
Controls.spikeCountTip: Number of spikes evenly distributed around the outer wall.
Controls.spawnCountTip: How many new balls spawn each time one escapes a wall.
Controls.targetCountTip: How many numbered segments to place on the wall.
Controls.randomOrderTip: Shuffle the position of target numbers around the wall.
Controls.colorCountTip: How many distinct colours are used on the wall segments. Fewer colours = easier to match.
Controls.ballSpeedTip: How fast the ball moves. Higher values make the simulation more energetic.
Controls.ballSizeTip: Radius of the ball in pixels. Larger balls have a harder time fitting through gaps.
Controls.gravityTip: Downward pull on the ball. Set to 0 for zero-gravity floating.
Controls.twoBallsTip: Spawn a second ball moving in the opposite direction for double the action.
Controls.bouncierTip: Every wall bounce adds (Bounciness − 1) × the Ball Speed to the rebound, with no ceiling: 1 = off, 1.03 = the classic Bouncier, 3 = +200 % a bounce, 1e6 = a million times. The ball keeps getting faster until it escapes – or breaks the page.
Controls.ballInteractionTip: What balls do to each other: bounce off (the default), merge into one bigger ball when they touch, split in two every time a ball breaks through a wall, or pass straight through each other. Deterministic: shared links, presets and Find Simulation include it.
Controls.interactionMergeDesc: Touching balls fuse into one ball with their combined area and momentum and a blended colour.
Controls.interactionSplitDesc: Every wall break splits the ball into two halves of half the area that fly apart – down to the smallest size and up to the ball cap.
Controls.interactionPassDesc: Balls ignore each other and fly straight through.
Controls.splitMinRadiusTip: A ball only splits while both halves would still be at least this big.
Controls.maxBallsTip: Splitting stops once this many balls are in play.
Controls.advancedPhysicsTip: Extra forces and wall behaviours. All of them are off by default, so a shared link or a found seed behaves exactly as before until you change them.
Controls.advancedPhysicsDesc: Deterministic extras: shared links, presets and Find Simulation include them.
Controls.airDragTip: Fraction of the ball's speed lost on every physics step (60 per second). A little makes the ball settle; a lot makes it sink.
Controls.windXTip: Constant sideways push, as a fraction of the ball speed gained every second. Negative blows left, positive right.
Controls.windYTip: Constant vertical push. Negative lifts the ball, positive presses it down.
Controls.spinStrengthTip: Wall contact makes the ball spin (rotating walls add their own twist) and the spin curves its flight like a Magnus effect. Custom ball images and emoji rotate with it.
Controls.rotatingGravityTip: Turns the direction of gravity by this many degrees per second, so "down" slowly circles around the arena.
Controls.wallBouncinessTip: How much speed the ball keeps when it rebounds off a wall. Below 100% every hit slows it down; above 100% every hit adds a kick.
Controls.breathingWallsTip: Walls grow and shrink around their normal size by this much; the gaps move with them.
Controls.breathingSpeedTip: How many pulses per second the walls breathe.
Controls.wallCountTip: Number of concentric circular walls the ball must break through.
Controls.wallThicknessTip: Thickness of each wall ring in pixels.
Controls.gapSizeTip: Size of the opening in each wall. Larger gaps make it easier for the ball to escape.
Controls.rotationTip: Walls rotate over time, making the gaps move around the circle.
Controls.trailsTip: Show a fading trail behind the ball as it moves.
Controls.ballGlowTip: Radial light effect around the ball.
Controls.wallGlowTip: Walls flash with colour when the ball bounces off them.
Controls.colorTrailTip: Rainbow hue-shifting trail behind the ball.
Controls.reactiveBgTip: Background pulses and shifts colour on each bounce.
Controls.cameraFollowTip: Smoothly shifts the viewport to keep the ball centred.
Controls.cinematicTip: Subtly steers rebounds to create near-misses and dramatic escapes. Turn off for pure physics.
Controls.trailThicknessTip: How thick the ball's trail is. Higher values create a bolder streak.
Controls.wallBreakEffectTip: Visual effect that plays when the ball breaks through a wall.
Controls.wallBreakSoundDesc: Play a custom audio clip instead of the default tones when the ball breaks through a wall.
Controls.hitSoundModeTip: What plays when the ball bounces off a wall: the synthesised tones (or a melody) or an audio clip of your own.
Controls.hitSampleDesc: Pick a built-in clip or upload your own. It plays on every wall bounce and is included in recordings.
Controls.hitSamplePitchByWallTip: Inner walls play the clip at a higher pitch and outer walls lower, following the same curve as the default tones.
Controls.hitSampleVolumeTip: Loudness of the hit sample relative to the other sounds.
Controls.hitSampleDecodeError: Could not decode this audio file – the synth tones play instead. Try an MP3, OGG, WAV or M4A file.
Controls.customSoundDesc: Choose a song to use its melody as bounce sounds. Each wall hit plays the next note from the song.
Controls.midiSourceText: Not sure where to get MIDI files? Try
Controls.midiParseError: Failed to parse MIDI file. Make sure it is a valid format 0 or 1 MIDI file.
Controls.sliceSongTip: The viral format: upload any song and every bounce plays the next little piece of it, so the ball "plays" the track.
Controls.sliceSongDesc: Upload an MP3, OGG, WAV or M4A file. Each wall hit plays the next slice of the song, continuing from where the last one stopped. The song stays in your browser.
Controls.sliceEnabledTip: While on, slices of the uploaded song replace the bounce tones and melody notes.
Controls.sliceLengthTip: How much of the song each bounce plays. Short slices sound choppy and rhythmic; long ones let whole phrases through.
Controls.sliceLoopTip: Start the song over when it reaches the end. When off, bounces go back to the default tones after the last slice.
Controls.sliceFadeTip: Fade-in and fade-out at the edges of every slice so the cuts don't click.
Controls.sliceDecodeError: Could not decode this audio file. Try an MP3, OGG, WAV or M4A file.
Controls.sliceNoSong: Upload a song to hear it – the default tones play until then.
Controls.musicBedTip: Mixes a music track under the bounce sounds and records it into the exported video, so the clip is ready to post. The file stays in your browser.
Controls.musicBedDesc: Upload an MP3, OGG, WAV or M4A file to play under the bounce sounds. It dips on every hit so the tones stay clear, then swells back. The track stays in your browser.
Controls.musicDecodeError: Could not decode this audio file. Try an MP3, OGG, WAV or M4A file.
Controls.wallBreakDecodeError: Could not decode this audio file – the wall breaks keep their default sound. Try an MP3, OGG, WAV or M4A file.
Controls.musicVolumeTip: How loud the music plays under the bounce sounds – in the speakers and in the exported video.
Controls.musicDuckingTip: How much the music dips on every bounce and wall break. 0% keeps it steady, 100% mutes it for an instant, like a sidechain compressor.
Controls.musicDuckReleaseTip: How long the music takes to swell back after a bounce, in milliseconds. Short is punchy, long is smooth.
Controls.musicLoopTip: Start the track again when it ends. Off: the music stops at the end of the track and stays silent until the next run.
Controls.musicStartOffsetTip: Skip the first seconds of the track so the drop lands right when the simulation starts. Restarts begin from here too.
Controls.instrumentDesc: The voice the wall tones are played with (a melody picks its own instrument below). Pluck, marimba and chip are synthesised live; the classic tone is Triangle.
Controls.melodyInstrumentDesc: The voice the notes of the chosen song are played with. Sine is the classic melody sound.
Controls.scaleDesc: Snap wall tones and melody notes to the nearest note of a scale so every bounce is in key. Chromatic keeps the original pitches.
Controls.beatLockTip: Delays each bounce sound to the next point of the beat grid (at most one grid step) so exports sit on the beat.
Controls.beatLockDesc: Play bounce sounds on a BPM grid; extra hits inside the same step are skipped so the rhythm stays clean.
Controls.durationTip: The simulation will automatically stop and save after this many seconds.
Controls.watermarkTip: Text displayed faintly in the centre of your exported recording.
Controls.saveHint: Save your current setup (colours, physics, effects) to use later.
Controls.presetLoadLocked: Finish or stop the batch render before loading a preset.
Controls.growthRateTip: How fast the ball grows with each bounce (as a percentage).
Controls.centerDotTip: Place a small dot in the centre of the circle that the ball bounces off.
Controls.growLinesTip: Draw lines from each bounce point to the ball, like in Lines mode.
Controls.dropDesc: Balls of different sizes and weights rain through rows of pegs and bars. Every hit plays a note pitched by the ball's size, so the run composes its own polyrhythm.
Controls.dropBallCountTip: How many balls are released from the top of the board.
Controls.dropSizeVariationTip: How far the ball sizes spread around the Ball Size setting. Bigger balls play lower notes.
Controls.dropGravityVariationTip: Gives every ball its own gravity, from floaty to heavy, so they fall out of step and the rhythm keeps shifting.
Controls.dropRowsTip: Number of staggered rows of pegs and bars between the top and the floor.
Controls.dropSpawnIntervalTip: Seconds between two balls leaving the top. 0 drops them all at once.
Controls.dropLoopTip: Opens the floor: balls that fall out of the bottom come back in at the top, so the piece never ends.
Controls.picturePaintTip: Upload any picture and the ball reveals it stroke by stroke – in rhythm with your song, steered so the whole picture appears, paced to finish when the song ends.
Controls.picturePaintDesc: PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF (first frame). The picture is fitted into the circle and stays in your browser; the ball's brush uncovers it and the run ends at 95 % revealed.
Controls.paintPictureError: Could not load this picture. Try a PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF file.
Controls.paintGhostTip: How visible the unrevealed part of the picture is, as a dim greyscale ghost, so viewers can guess what is coming.
Controls.paintBrushTip: Radius of each brush dab as a multiple of the ball. Pace to Song still resizes it to finish on time.
Controls.paintBeatSyncTip: The ball speeds up on every beat and glides in between; the brush and the glow pulse with it. Deterministic, so a recording replays exactly.
Controls.paintBeatSyncDesc: Moves the ball in rhythm: a kick on each beat, a glide until the next. Needs a song with a detectable beat or the manual BPM.
Controls.paintNoSong: Upload a song (Background Music or Song Slicer in the Custom Sound section) to detect its beat, or use the manual BPM.
Controls.paintNoBeat: No steady beat found in this song – use the manual BPM.
Controls.paintBeatPulseTip: How hard each beat kicks the ball: 0 % glides evenly, 100 % doubles the speed on the beat.
Controls.paintGuidedTip: Turns every rebound a little (up to 18°) toward the largest unrevealed area, so the whole picture appears instead of one corner.
Controls.paintGuidedDesc: Meticulous: rebounds aim at what is still hidden.
Controls.paintPaceTip: Resizes the brush every second so the reveal finishes when the song – or the clip – ends. The HUD shows whether the ball is on schedule.
Controls.paintPaceDesc: Finish the reveal with the song (or with the clip length without one).
Controls.dropLoopDesc: Off: the run ends once every ball has come to rest on the floor.
Controls.boxDesc: A box instead of rings. Squares, circles or DVD-style logos fly in straight lines and every wall hit plays a note: the next note of the melody, or one of four notes per wall without one. The numbers count down per bounce, colours cycle and the shapes grow a little.
Controls.boxShapeTip: What bounces around the box: axis-aligned squares, circles or a rounded DVD-style logo whose corner hits are accented with a louder note and a flash.
Controls.boxShapeCountTip: How many shapes start from the centre of the box. They pass through each other, so their rhythms never disturb one another.
Controls.boxSpeedRatioTip: Speeds of the shapes in small whole-number ratios: with 2:3 the second shape hits the walls three times while the first hits twice – that is the polyrhythm. With 1:1 every shape gets its own launch angle instead. The fastest shape moves at the Ball Speed times the seed's tempo (±15 %), which is what lets Find Simulation hit an exact clip length.
Controls.boxSpeedRatioDesc: The launch angle is chosen so each shape's top/bottom and left/right hits form a small ratio of their own. A DVD logo always gets an odd ratio and is re-aimed by a hair at every bounce, so it reaches a corner exactly every 3–13 hits – even while it grows.
Controls.boxCountdownTip: The number on every shape counts down by one per wall hit and the run ends when every shape reaches zero. 0 switches the countdown off and the shapes bounce forever.
Controls.boxGrowPerHitTip: How much a shape grows with every wall hit, as a percentage of its size (capped so it never fills the box).
Controls.boxGravityTip: How much of the Gravity setting acts on the shapes. 0 is the classic straight-line DVD motion; anything above turns the shapes into bouncing balls that keep their bounce height.
Controls.boxAspectTip: Width of the box relative to its height: 9:16 fills a vertical clip, 1:1 is a square, 16:9 is landscape.
Controls.pwDesc: Pendulums tuned like the classic pendulum wave: the slowest swings K times per cycle and each next one once more, so the row drifts into travelling waves, splits into groups and snaps back in line at the end of every cycle. Every centre crossing plays a note pitched by the pendulum's place in the row.
Controls.pwLayoutTip: Where the pendulums hang: a row under a bar (strings visibly different in length), an arc of pivots swinging toward the centre, bobs moving along radii from the centre (optionally on a rotating polygon), the same on a slowly turning frame that draws spiral arms, bobs sliding on rails, or balls bouncing on a floor with periods in the same series.
Controls.pwPolygonTip: Maps the bobs of the Circle and Galaxy layouts onto the outline of a polygon that turns once per cycle, instead of a circle.
Controls.pwCountTip: How many pendulums swing side by side. More pendulums make finer waves and richer chords; the notes climb a major scale from the slowest one.
Controls.pwBaseOscillationsTip: Swings the slowest pendulum completes per cycle (the classic Harvard wave uses 51). Every next pendulum completes one more, which is what tunes the row to realign exactly once per cycle. Lower numbers give a slow, sparse wave; higher ones a fast, dense one.
Controls.pwCycleSecondsTip: Seconds until the row is back in line. The run ends after the chosen number of cycles.
Controls.pwAmplitudeTip: Swing amplitude in degrees. Wider swings shorten the row's strings so the outermost bobs still fit; the radial and sliding layouts travel further. Bouncing balls ignore it – their heights follow the periods.
Controls.pwPhasingTip: Off: the classic tuning, every pendulum in line again at the end of each cycle. On: the swing times form an arithmetic series (each pendulum's swing lasts a fixed bit longer than the next one's) – a Reich-style tempo phase shift that keeps drifting instead of snapping back.
Controls.pwTrailsTip: How long the fading trails of the bobs last; the spiral arms of the Galaxy layout live in them.
Controls.pwSoundOnTip: When a pendulum sounds: crossing the centre line (twice per swing), reaching an extreme, or both. Bouncing balls play on the floor hit and at the apex.
Controls.pwPitchDirectionTip: Low to high: the slowest (longest) pendulum plays the lowest note. High to low: the other way round. The notes are degrees of a major scale from C4 and are snapped to the scale chosen in the Sound section.
Controls.pwWaveChordTip: Bobs that align within 20 ms play together as one chord – one sound on the beat grid, the level shared out – instead of a pile of separate notes. A chord of most of the row is accented with a flash.
Controls.pwCyclesTip: Full cycles after which the run finishes, with the whole row back in line. 0 keeps it swinging forever.
Controls.finderDesc: Find a simulation seed that runs for the exact duration you select, keeping all your custom settings in mind.
Controls.topTextTip: Custom text overlay displayed above the physics arena.
Controls.bottomTextTip: Custom text overlay displayed below the physics arena.
Controls.textSizeTip: Adjust the font size of the text overlays.
Controls.findSimulationTip: Search for a simulation seed that produces a run of the exact target duration.
Controls.seedProgressDeeper: Seed {tested} · searching deeper, up to {left}s more
Controls.fixedRunLength: Always {duration}s with these settings – change the cycle length or the cycles
Controls.characterTip: Give the ball a personality: a face that looks where it flies, blinks and reacts to hits, breaking walls and escapes, plus a name under it. Purely visual – seeds and found simulations are not affected.
Controls.ballFaceTip: A vector face drawn on the ball (and in the recording). The eyes follow the flight, blink on a seeded schedule, squint on hard hits, go wide when a wall breaks, grin at the escape and close happily at rest.
Controls.ballNameTip: A small name label drawn under the (first) ball, e.g. Gerald.
Controls.nameLabelTip: Show the name under the ball, with a subtle outline so it reads on any background.
Controls.ballSquashTip: The ball squashes against whatever it hits and springs back into shape. Visual only – the physics does not change.
Controls.faceOverImageTip: Draw the face over a custom ball image or emoji as well (off keeps the picture's own face).
Controls.faceSoundsTip: The cat face chirps a synthesised meow when it gets hit, when a wall breaks and when it escapes – on the beat grid and in the recording. Not used while the bounce sound is an audio sample.
Controls.faceSoundsSampleNote: Silent while the bounce sound is an audio sample – switch back to tones to hear the cat.
Controls.geraldPersonaDesc: Gerald always escapes – freedom lasts about 4 seconds. One click sets his face, name and squash.
Controls.themeTip: One-click looks: a theme sets the wall, ball, line, background and trail colours and the particle style. Every colour stays editable afterwards – click the theme again to restore it.
Controls.themeEdited: edited – click it again to restore
Controls.themeBackgroundTip: A solid colour, a top-to-bottom gradient or your own picture behind the arena. The reactive background still flashes on top, and exports continue it into the letterbox bars.
Controls.themeBgError: This picture could not be loaded. Try a PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF file.
Controls.themeBgImageNote: The picture is cover-fitted behind the arena. It stays in your browser and is not part of shared links or presets.
Controls.themeBgDimTip: Darkens the background picture so the balls and walls stand out.
Controls.themeParticlesTip: What bursts out when a wall breaks or a run finishes. With a theme picked, the particles take its colours.
Controls.themeTrailTip: The colour trail flows between two colours of your choice instead of the rainbow.
Controls.prDesc: Voices ticking at their own tempos: every tick plays a note, and whenever all of them tick together the screen flashes and a chord sounds. Positions are exact functions of time, so even 400 voices replay identically.
Controls.prLayoutTip: Rings: a dot on each ring orbits a whole number of times per cycle and ticks at 12 o'clock. Arcs: dots slide back and forth across a circle and tick at both ends. Metronomes: a grid of pendulums ticking at both extremes – pair it with the BPM steps for a tempo phase shift. Spiral: orbiting dots whose tick points lie on a spiral, redrawn at every alignment. You can switch the layout mid-run; the rhythm carries on.
Controls.prArcStyleTip: Chords: every dot slides along its own horizontal chord of a big circle (the "metronomes inside a circle" look). Semicircles: every dot swings along a half circle and ticks on the baseline.
Controls.prPolygonTip: Draws every ring as a polygon with as many corners as its ratio (3 ticks per cycle = a triangle), turning once per cycle so a corner meets the dot at every tick.
Controls.prTemposTip: Harmonic: voice n ticks n times per cycle (1:2:3…), all in phase at the end of every cycle. BPM steps: the tempos climb from a base BPM by a fixed step, so neighbours drift apart slowly and line up again only after a long time. Custom: your own list of ratios such as 3,4,5,7.
Controls.prCountTip: How many voices tick at once, up to 400. More voices make denser patterns; the notes climb a major scale from the slowest one.
Controls.prCycleSecondsTip: Seconds per cycle for the harmonic and custom tempos: a voice with ratio n ticks n times per cycle, and every voice is in phase again at the end of each cycle.
Controls.prBaseBpmTip: Tempo of the first voice, in beats per minute.
Controls.prBpmStepTip: How much faster each next voice ticks, in BPM. Small steps give a slow Reich-style phase shift; the voices line up again once every tempo fits a whole number of ticks into the same time.
Controls.prCustomTip: Whole numbers separated by commas, spaces or colons – each one is a voice ticking that many times per cycle (3:4:5 is the classic polyrhythm). Up to 400 voices.
Controls.prAccentEveryTip: Makes every k-th tick of each voice louder and longer, with a ring around the dot – like the first beat of a bar. 0 turns accents off.
Controls.prPitchByTip: By voice: each voice plays the next degree of a major scale from C4. By ratio: each voice plays its tempo ratio as a harmonic of C3, so 3:4:5 sounds like the chord G–C–E. Both are snapped to the scale chosen in the Sound section.
Controls.prNumbersTip: Writes each voice's ratio (or BPM) on its dot.
Controls.prCyclesTip: Cycles after which the run ends, with every voice back in phase. 0 keeps it ticking forever.
Controls.cpDesc: Hundreds of orbs of different sizes bounce off the walls and off each other – mass follows size – and every collision plays a soft note pitched by the smaller orb: big orbs low, small orbs high.
Controls.cpCountTip: How many orbs collide, from 10 to 2000. They are sized automatically to fill the container (Ball Size makes them bigger or smaller); the ring holds at most 36 lollipops.
Controls.cpSizeSpreadTip: How different the orbs are: 0 makes them all the same size, 100% spreads them from a third to three times the base size. Mass follows the area, so big orbs shove small ones around – and bigger orbs play lower notes.
Controls.cpContainerTip: The shape the orbs bounce around in: a circle or a square, both filling the centre of the video.
Controls.cpGravityTip: How much of the Gravity setting pulls the orbs down. 0 is a floating gas of orbs; higher values heap them up at the bottom while they keep bouncing.
Controls.cpRestitutionTip: Coefficient of restitution of every collision: 1 is perfectly elastic (the orbs never lose energy), 0.7 is soft and damped, so under gravity the orbs settle into a pile.
Controls.cpSquishyTip: Squash and stretch: every impact flattens an orb along the direction of the hit for a split second (120 ms), like a jelly ball. Purely visual.
Controls.cpSyncStartTip: All orbs start on a grid at the same instant – from rest under gravity, or all flying the same way without it – so they fall and bounce in sync. Pair it with Squishy and a Size Variety of 0 for the “squishy balls bounce in sync” clip.
Controls.cpAntiCollisionAtTip: Second of the run at which the collision system switches off: the orbs change colour and pass straight through each other (they still bounce off the container). Off keeps them colliding forever.
Controls.cpRingTip: Constrains the bodies to a circular track: each one is a lollipop – a stick from the centre to a disc – that collides with its neighbours along the ring. With gravity they swing like pendulums around the bottom.
Controls.ballCountTip: How many balls start in the arena, flying out in evenly spread directions (Classic, Multiply, Lines, Shatter and Color Match, up to six; Grow, whose balls grow to fill the ring, up to two; Multiply multiplies them from there). Two is the old two-ball setup; with teams, every ball is a team.
Controls.teamsTip: Give every ball a team: a name, a colour and an emoji. The canvas labels the balls, keeps score per team (bounces, walls broken, escapes) and crowns a winner when the run ends – in the recording too. Winner: most escapes, then most walls broken, then most bounces.
Controls.teamsModeNote: Teams play in the modes with several balls: Classic, Multiply, Lines, Shatter, Color Match and Grow.
Controls.teamsModeCapNote: This mode plays with at most {max} balls: the first {max} teams play, the others wait for another mode.
Controls.showBallNamesTip: Show each team's name above its ball.
Controls.showScoreboardTip: Bounces, walls broken and escapes of every team in a corner of the video, the leader on top.
Controls.scoreboardPositionTip: The corner of the exported square the scoreboard sits in.
Controls.cameraGroupTip: Cinematic camera effects. They only change the picture and the pace at which the clock feeds the simulation, never the physics: seeds and found simulations play out exactly the same.
Controls.cameraGroupDesc: Zoom in on the ball, shake the view when a wall breaks, slow down on near misses and replay the escape – in the preview and in recordings.
Controls.cameraZoomTip: How far the view zooms toward the ball, following it around the arena. 0 keeps today's view (with Camera Follow on, the gentle classic follow). With several balls (Ball Count) the zoom stays wide enough to keep them all in frame.
Controls.screenShakeTip: Shakes the view every time a wall breaks; the shake dies out over 300 ms. Higher values shake harder.
Controls.slowMoOnNearMissTip: When the ball squeezes through a gap right next to its edge (the Drama Director's near miss), time slows down for a moment. The simulation runs the same steps, just slower – recordings show the slow motion.
Controls.slowMoFactorTip: How fast time runs during the slow motion: 0.2× is very slow, 0.8× barely slower.
Controls.slowMoMsTip: How long each slow-motion moment lasts, in real time. Afterwards a short pause keeps back-to-back near misses from slowing down the whole run.
Controls.replayOnEscapeTip: When a ball escapes the outer wall and the run ends, its last 2 seconds play again at half speed with a REPLAY badge before the end screen – in recordings too.
Controls.replayOnEscapeModes: The replay plays in the escape modes: Classic, Accumulation, Portal, Shatter and Color Match.
Controls.glassDesc: Stages of glass panes stand between the ball and HOME. Every landing cracks a pane and plays the next note (the next melody note, or a scale degree by row); the last hit shatters it with the wall-break sound – a glass clip unless you pick another. Each new stage brings more panes, thicker ones, sliding ones and ones with holes.
Controls.glassRowsTip: How many glass panes the first stage holds, from 3 to 30. Every later stage adds a third more (up to 30), packed closer together, so the hits speed up as the ball gets deeper.
Controls.glassHpTip: How many landings a pane of the first stage takes before it shatters, from 1 to 5; every hit grows another crack from the impact point. Every other stage the glass gets one hit thicker (at most two more).
Controls.glassStagesTip: How many stages the ball smashes through before it reaches HOME, from 1 to 10. The camera scrolls down to each new stage and a banner announces it.
Controls.glassMovingTip: From the third stage on, some panes are narrower and slide left and right: the ball can miss one and drop past it – a lucky escape – or bounce up into it from below.
Controls.glassHolesTip: From the second stage on, some panes have a hole the ball must miss to keep smashing. Dropping through it skips that pane (the ball can still crack it from below).
Controls.glassGatesTip: A row of three gates above every stage's glass – x2 DMG (a pane loses two hit points a hit), x1.5 SPEED (every hop runs faster) and x1.25 SIZE – in a seeded order. The gate Gerald falls through stacks its multiplier on him (with no cap unless you set one in the Ball section's Multipliers group) and the HUD shows it.
Controls.glassRunSize: Whole run: {panes} panes and up to {hits} hits over {stages} stage(s), then HOME.
Controls.mpDesc: Speed, size, damage, bounce and gravity multipliers stack on the ball – with no cap unless you set one. Pickups float in the ring modes, and a ball whose damage reaches the smash level breaks the rings it touches.
Controls.multiplierPickupsTip: Floating orbs – x2 SPEED, x1.5 SIZE, x2 DMG, x2 BALLS… – appear at seeded times and places inside the ball's ring. Touching one stacks it on the ball with a burst, a rising arpeggio and a pop of the HUD badge. Seeds and Find Simulation include them.
Controls.pickupRateTip: How many orbs appear per 10 seconds on average (0–3).
Controls.pickupTypesTip: Which orbs may appear. x2 BALLS clones the ball (up to the Ball Cap of the ball interaction) and only floats in the modes that play with several balls.
Controls.pickupBallsUnavailable: x2 BALLS only floats in Classic, Multiply, Lines, Shatter and Grow.
Controls.pickupLifetimeTip: Seconds an orb drifts before it fades away.
Controls.mpUnlimitedTip: On (default): multipliers stack without any cap – the speed can keep doubling. The physics stays safe at any value: more sub-steps per frame, and past 64 the clock slows down (SLOW-MO) instead of letting a ball tunnel through a wall.
Controls.mpCapTip: With Unlimited off: the highest value any stat may stack to (and 1/cap the lowest). 0 = no cap.
Controls.wallSmashThresholdTip: Once a ball's damage multiplier reaches this value it smashes the rings it touches – no gap needed – with the wall-break effect and sound (Classic, Accumulation, Multiply, Shatter, Color Match, Portal).
Controls.mpBoardDesc: Balls fall through rows of gates to HOME: count gates clone them, speed, size and damage gates stack multipliers, ÷2 takes half away and release doors let them through in bursts.
Controls.mpRowsTip: Rows of gates between the start and HOME, 4 to 20. The camera scrolls down with the lowest ball.
Controls.mpStartBallsTip: Balls released at the top, 1 to 10.
Controls.mpMaxBallsTip: Most balls in play at once (50–2000): count gates stop cloning there. Balls that reach HOME free their place.
Controls.mpGateMixTip: How often each kind of gate appears, relative to the others (0 = never). The slider covers 0–9; the field next to it takes any weight (40, 0.5, 1e6). The layout itself is drawn from the seed.
Controls.mpTargetTip: Rigging: with a target, Find Simulation searches for a seed whose final HOME count is within 5 % of it (instead of a duration). 0 = off.
Controls.obstaclesTip: Place pegs, bumpers, blockers and spinners inside the arena. Positions and sizes scale with the canvas and are saved in the share link and in presets.
Controls.obstaclesEmpty: No obstacles yet – pick a type and add one.
Controls.obstaclesMax: That is the maximum of {max} obstacles.
Controls.bumperBoostTip: How much faster a ball flies off a bumper: every hit multiplies its speed by this – no cap, so hit after hit it keeps getting faster (the field takes any boost).
Controls.obstacleHint: Before the start or while paused, drag an obstacle on the canvas to move it; click one and press Backspace (or ✕ in the Obstacles list) to delete it.
Controls.obstaclesModeNote: Obstacles play in the ring modes, such as Classic, Shatter or Portal. Your layout is kept for when you switch back to one.
Controls.captionsDesc: Animated overlays for the clip: a countdown, a wall counter, a progress bar, a question that reveals its answer, or your own text. They are drawn on the canvas, so every recording includes them.
Controls.captionsTip: Each caption enters and leaves with a fade, slide or pop animation between its start and end time. The timing runs on the simulation clock: pausing holds the captions, 8× plays them eight times faster and Restart starts them over. While a clip is recorded, the countdown and the progress bar count the clip itself, from Record Video to the end of the recording. Captions travel in the share link and are saved in presets.
Controls.captionsEmpty: No captions yet – add one below.
Controls.captionAddTip: Adds a caption of that type (up to {max}). Captions at the same position stack in the order of the list.
Controls.captionsClipNote: The countdown and the progress bar run to the clip length set in Recording ({duration}s).
Controls.captionTypeTip: Countdown: the time left to the end of the clip. Wall counter: walls broken out of the walls in play ("Wall 3/10"; hidden in the modes without rings). Progress bar: the elapsed time over the clip length. Question: a question whose answer pops in when a ball escapes or the run finishes. Text: any text.
Controls.captionTextTip: The text to show (up to 80 characters; a long text wraps onto up to three lines).
Controls.captionQuestionTip: The question to show, e.g. "Will it escape?" – an empty field shows that one.
Controls.captionCountdownLabelTip: Optional text around the time: [time] is replaced by the time left ("[time] left"); a label without it goes in front of the time.
Controls.captionWallLabelTip: Optional text instead of "Wall [n]/[total]": [n] is the walls broken and [total] the walls in play; a label without them goes in front of the count.
Controls.captionProgressLabelTip: Optional text above the bar; [pct] is replaced by the elapsed percentage.
Controls.captionAnswerTip: Revealed under the question the moment a ball escapes or the run finishes – it pops in and stays until the end. Leave it empty to show the question only.
Controls.captionPositionTip: Top, center or bottom of the exported square. Captions at the same position stack; the top and bottom ones keep clear of the scoreboard and of the Top / Bottom Text.
Controls.captionStartTip: Second of the run (simulation time) at which the caption enters.
Controls.captionEndTip: Second at which the caption has left. 0 – or any time not after the start – keeps it until the end of the run.
Controls.captionAnimationTip: How the caption enters and leaves: fades in and out, slides in from its edge of the frame, or pops in with a bounce.
Controls.captionSizeTip: Text size, 0.5× to 3×; the progress bar gets thicker too.
Controls.captionBackgroundTip: A rounded box behind the text (the track of the progress bar). Off: the text gets a soft shadow instead.
Controls.riggedGroupTip: Guaranteed results for storytelling clips. The drama director enforces them on top of the physics – deterministically, so seeds, found simulations and recordings replay exactly the same.
Controls.riggedWarning: For storytelling only: these switches decide how the run ends. Clips made with them are staged – don't pass them off as real physics.
Controls.neverEscapeTip: No ball ever leaves the outer wall: the director steers every rebound away from its gap – plenty of near misses – and the last wall holds even when a ball does reach the gap. The escape modes then never end, so set the clip length in the Recording section.
Controls.neverEscapeModes: No effect in this mode – its balls cannot escape anyway. It works in Classic, Accumulation, Multiply, Portal, Shatter and Color Match.
Controls.forcedWinnerTip: The chosen ball – its team – always wins: the other balls cannot get through a wall before it has, and the director steers its rebounds toward the gaps. It breaks the walls first and escapes first, so it tops the scoreboard.
Controls.forcedWinnerModes: Needs two balls or more (Ball Count or a team roster) in Classic, Multiply, Shatter or Color Match.
Controls.forcedWinnerNeverEscape: Off while Never Escape is on: in this mode the chosen team wins by escaping, and nobody escapes. Together with Never Escape the Forced Winner works in Classic, where the walls it breaks first decide.
Controls.timelineDesc: Automate settings over the clip: pick a setting, set its value and add a keyframe at the current time. Between two keyframes the value glides in a straight line; before the first and after the last it holds.
Controls.timelineTip: Keyframes run on the simulation clock: a pause holds them, 8× plays them faster and Restart starts them over, so Find Simulation and the recording see the same run. They drive the run only – your own slider values stay as they are and come back when a setting's keyframes are removed.
Controls.timelineSettingTip: The setting the next keyframe drives. While a setting has keyframes, its slider shows the live value with an AUTO badge and is locked.
Controls.timelineValueTip: The setting's own value – the value the next keyframe gets (the same as its slider in the panel).
Controls.timelineAddTip: Adds a keyframe of the picked setting at the simulation's current time (0 s before the start) with the value above; one already at that time is replaced.
Controls.timelineEmpty: No keyframes yet – every setting keeps its slider value.
Controls.timelineRotationOff: Rotation is switched off in the Wall Settings
Controls.timelineClipNote: The bar under the canvas spans the clip ({duration} s): a lane per automated setting with its keyframes, and the playhead at the simulation clock. Values glide between keyframes and hold outside them.
Controls.timelineAutoTip: Automated by the timeline: the value follows its keyframes. Edit them in the Timeline section.
Controls.dpDesc: Chaotic double pendulums swing over a harp: every string a bob crosses is plucked and plays its note, while the last bob paints a long rainbow trail. Add pendulums for the butterfly effect, a third arm for a triple pendulum, or let two pendulums spar.
Controls.dpSegmentsTip: Two arms make the classic double pendulum; a third arm makes a triple pendulum – even wilder, with a whip at the end.
Controls.dpCountTip: How many pendulums hang from the same pivot. Each one starts a hair (0.05°) further than the last: they swing as one at first and then fly apart – the butterfly effect. Sparring always uses two.
Controls.dpSparTip: Two pendulums hang side by side, start as mirror images and their bobs collide elastically: every hit plays a low, percussive note and flashes – a hard one lights up the whole frame.
Controls.dpRandomStartTip: On: every run starts from a high, chaotic position drawn from the seed – Restart for a new one; a found seed or a shared link replays it exactly. Off: the start angles below.
Controls.dpAngleTip: Where the arm starts, in degrees from hanging straight down (180° is straight up). Sparring mirrors the angles for the second pendulum.
Controls.dpLengthTip: Relative length of the arm. The whole pendulum is scaled to fill the video, so only the proportions matter: a short first arm makes the last bob loop around the pivot.
Controls.dpMassTip: Mass of the bob. A heavy first bob with a light last one makes the end whip around; heavier bobs are drawn a little bigger (and hit harder when sparring).
Controls.dpGravityTip: Gravity as a multiple of Earth's on a 1 m pendulum: lower is slow and dreamy, higher is fast and frantic.
Controls.dpDampingTip: How much of its speed the pendulum loses every second, until it hangs still. Off keeps it swinging forever – the integrator holds the energy for the whole clip.
Controls.dpTrailSecondsTip: How many seconds back the rainbow trail of the last bob reaches, fading out towards its end. Off hides it (so does the Trails switch of the Visual Effects section).
Controls.dpStringsTip: Strings across the video. Every bob that crosses a string plucks it: the string vibrates and plays its note, tuned to the scale and root note of the Custom Sound section (a major scale while the scale is chromatic), low to high. The instrument, the beat lock and hit samples apply. Off: no harp.
Controls.dpStringLayoutTip: Vertical strings side by side with the low notes on the left, or radial strings around the centre that rise clockwise.
Controls.dpOctavesTip: How many octaves the strings span from the root note of the Custom Sound section: the first string is the root, the last one the root this many octaves up.
Controls.dpEndlessTip: Off: the run ends with a chord after the clip length (the Duration of the Recording section). On: the pendulums swing until you stop them.
Controls.dpFixedRunLength: Always {duration}s – the clip length; change the Duration or switch Endless on
Controls.ilDesc: Four circle illusions in the style of project.jdm. Every touch, bounce and collision plays a note through your instrument, scale and beat lock.
Controls.ilTypeTip: Lines: balls sliding back and forth on straight lines that together roll a hidden circle. Rings: one ball bouncing in every ring while the rings turn. Nested: circles bouncing inside circles, with wobbly walls. White spaces: balls paint the arena and leave a hidden picture white.
Controls.ilHintLines: Each ball only slides back and forth along its diameter – yet together they form a smaller circle rolling around inside the big one.
Controls.ilHintRings: Every ring holds one ball bouncing between its walls. The rings turn at different speeds, so the bounces ripple outward in spirals and line up again at the end of every cycle.
Controls.ilHintNested: A circle bouncing inside a circle inside a circle – every hit pushes the next one along and makes its wall wobble.
Controls.ilHintWhitespace: The balls paint the white arena black but can never enter the hidden shapes: the white spaces left at the end are the picture.
Controls.ilBallsTip: Balls on diameters, 2–32. Ball i slides along the diameter at angle i·π/N with a phase offset of i·π/N, so all of them sit on one smaller circle rolling inside the big one. Each plays its own note when it touches the rim.
Controls.ilRingsTip: Concentric rings with one ball each, 2–16. The inner rings turn faster and play higher notes.
Controls.ilDepthTip: Moving circles inside the arena, 2–5: each one bounces inside the next bigger one and the smallest is the ball. The collisions are elastic, so the energy passes back and forth between the layers.
Controls.ilPaintersTip: Balls painting the arena, 1–12. More painters reveal the picture sooner; the run ends when the arena is painted.
Controls.ilPatternTip: The shape the balls can never enter. Auto lets the seed choose, so every seed can hide a different picture.
Controls.ilSpeedTip: Tempo of the illusion: at 1× a lines cycle takes 4 s and a rings cycle 24 s; the nested circles and the painters speed up or slow down with it.
Controls.ilTracksTip: Lines: draw the diameters the balls slide on. Rings: draw the rail each ball rides on.
Controls.ilRevealTip: Lines: show the hidden circle the balls form as it rolls. Rings: draw a line through the balls to show the travelling pattern.
Controls.ilCyclesTip: Lines and rings: the run finishes after this many cycles, with every ball back where it started. Never keeps it going.
Controls.wallWobbleTip: Circular walls bulge where a ball hits them; the bulge travels round the wall and dies away like jelly. Visual only – the physics, seeds and Find Simulation stay the same.
Controls.sbDesc: oddplayground's WEB DOMINION: every wall bounce anchors a glowing thread from the ring to the ball, the threads follow their balls, and the combat rule decides who pays for crossing them. The last ball standing wins.
Controls.sbRuleTip: Cut: a ball crossing an enemy thread – anywhere from the ring to the ball it hangs on – cuts it and the thread's owner loses a life. Touch: the threads are lasers – a ball touching an enemy thread anywhere loses a life itself. Collide: ball-to-ball collisions cost the slower ball a life (every ring bounce sets a ball's speed afresh, so the slower one changes from clash to clash). After a lost life a ball is shielded for a moment.
Controls.sbHintCut: Crossing an enemy thread cuts it – its owner loses a life, and its web is shielded for 2.5 s.
Controls.sbHintTouch: The threads are lasers: touching an enemy thread costs the toucher a life.
Controls.sbHintCollide: Ball-to-ball hits cost the slower ball a life; the threads are decoration.
Controls.sbStyleTip: Web: numbered balls, thread segments and the WEB DOMINION HUD. Neon: every thread is an endless line painted additively across the canvas (moiré art), the ring wobbles like jelly behind coloured outline rings, and every lost life glitches the frame.
Controls.sbHintWeb: Numbered balls, glowing thread segments and the WEB DOMINION HUD.
Controls.sbHintNeon: #neonphysics: endless lines paint moiré art, the ring wobbles like jelly and every lost life glitches the frame.
Controls.sbBallsTip: How many balls fight, 2–6. A roster in Teams & Scoreboard gives the first ones its colours and names; the rest use the neon palette.
Controls.sbLivesTip: Lives every ball starts with, 1–9 – the number on the ball. A ball at 0 shatters and its threads dissolve.
Controls.sbMaxStringsTip: How many threads a ball drags at most, 3–40; beyond that the oldest one detaches and fades.
Controls.sbDurationTip: Judge the battle after this many seconds: the survivors with the most lives win (then the most kills, then the most bounces). Off: the battle goes on until one ball remains.
Controls.sbFinaleSpeedTip: When two balls are left and one of them is a cut from elimination (or the clip limit is 6 s away) the balls speed up to this and their halos strobe – the end gets intense.
Controls.sbWobbleTip: Neon style: how much the ring wobbles like jelly on every hit (visual only).
Controls.sbBadgeTip: The "FLASHING LIGHTS – THE END GETS INTENSE" badge in the top-left corner of the clip.
Controls.sbHudTip: Web style: a row per ball in the top-right corner – colour, name, kill pips and ×kills – with the threads alive below, and a dashed ring around a ball that is one cut from elimination.
Controls.sbRosterNote: The first {count} of {balls} balls wear the Teams & Scoreboard roster; the rest use the neon palette.
Controls.sbPaletteNote: Palette: {names} – or set a roster in Teams & Scoreboard.
Controls.plDesc: A stack of rainbow layers stands between the ball and freedom. Every hit on the stack destroys as many layers as the power, then the power advances by the sequence – x2 by default – and the next note of the scale plays. The ball bounces on a steady beat and speeds up as the stack drops; when the last layer shatters it falls out of the bottom.
Controls.plLayersTip: How many thin rainbow layers the stack holds, from 20 to 800. With the power doubling on every hit, 120 layers fall in 7 hits and 800 in 10.
Controls.plSequenceTip: How the power grows after every hit: doubling (1, 2, 4, 8 …), Fibonacci (1, 1, 2, 3, 5 …), the primes (2, 3, 5, 7 …), +1 per hit (1, 2, 3 …) or chaos – every power drawn from the seed between 0 and twice the best so far, so some hits destroy dozens of layers and others change nothing.
Controls.plHintRandom: Powers: 1, then anything from 0 to twice the record – the seed decides.
Controls.plDriftTip: How much the ball drifts sideways as it bounces, from 0 (straight up and down) to 1. Every hit gives it a small seeded kick so the loop stays alive; the drift never moves the moment a hit lands.
Controls.plSpeedTip: Bounces per second, from 0.5× to 2× (one a second at 1×). Every bounce takes exactly the same time however deep the stack is – the ball simply flies faster – so a run lasts the hit count × the bounce period.
Controls.plBadgeTip: The small badge in the top-left corner of the playfield: SOUND ON, the FLASHING LIGHTS / THE END GETS INTENSE warning, both, or none.
Controls.plPillsTip: The two rainbow pills at the top: the rule with the current power (“Each hit x2 the power · power 16”) and the level with “new sound every level”.
Controls.plRunInfo: {hits} hits × {period}s a bounce, then freedom: every run lasts {seconds}s.
Controls.plRunChaos: Chaos: the seed decides the hit count ({period}s a bounce), so the Simulation Finder can search for a length.
Controls.plFixedRunLength: Always {duration}s with these settings – change the layers, the sequence or the bounce speed
Controls.fastExportFpsTip: Frames per second of the Fast export: 60 is the smoothest, 30 makes a smaller file and renders sooner. The physics always runs 60 steps a second, so the run and its sounds are the same either way.
Controls.projectFilesDesc: Save the whole setup – every setting with its obstacles, keyframes, captions and teams, plus the pictures and sounds you uploaded – in one .jumpingballslive.json file, and open it again later or on another computer.
Controls.projectMediaNone: No uploaded media – the file holds the settings only.
Controls.projectLargeWarning: {size} of media is more than {limit}: the file will be slow to save and to send. Shorter or compressed songs make it smaller.
Controls.projectLargeConfirm: The media in this project add up to {size}, more than {limit}. Export it anyway?
Controls.projectTooLarge: The media add up to {size}; a project holds at most {max}. Remove the largest song or picture and try again.
Controls.projectDropHint: You can also drop a .jumpingballslive.json file anywhere on this panel.
Controls.projectDropHere: Drop the project file to open it
Controls.projectImportLocked: A render is running – finish or stop the batch (or the fast export) before opening a project.
Controls.projectImportedSkipped: Opened “{name}”, but {count} damaged media file(s) were left out.
Controls.projectErrorNotJson: This file is not a project file (it is not valid JSON).
Controls.projectErrorNotProject: This file is not a {siteName} project.
Controls.projectErrorNewer: This project was saved by a newer version of the simulator. Reload the page to get the latest version and try again.
Controls.projectErrorTooLarge: This project is too large to open (at most {max} of media).
Controls.projectErrorNotFile: “{file}” is not a project file – choose a .jumpingballslive.json file.
Controls.projectErrorRead: The project could not be opened.
Controls.projectExportError: The project could not be saved.
Controls.rcDesc: Racers drop down a long track generated from the seed: pegs, funnels, spinners, pinball bumpers, turbo pads, narrow gates and swap zones. Every obstacle hit is the racer's note, every overtake a chime; the winner gets a fanfare and a podium.
Controls.rcRacersTip: How many racers line up on the start grid (2–16). Racers 1–6 take the names, colours and emoji of the Teams roster; the others race in colours of their own.
Controls.rcShapeTip: Squares tumble as they slide; circles look like marbles. Both collide as circles, so the race is the same.
Controls.rcRosterNote: Names, colours and emoji of the first six racers come from the Teams & Scoreboard tab.
Controls.rcTrackLengthTip: Length of one lap in screens (the height of the video). A longer track makes a longer race – about two seconds per screen.
Controls.rcLapsTip: The lap's rows come round again this many times – a looping track. Every lap ends in the same final sector: a swap zone and a turbo strip.
Controls.rcFeatureTip: Which obstacles the track is built from: everything, or one kind featured in about half of the rows. The cup is named after it unless you give it a title.
Controls.rcCameraTip: Follow the leader (it stays in the lower part of the view, the pack behind it) or frame the whole pack from the leader to the last racer.
Controls.rcStandingsTip: Positions, names and gaps to the leader in the top-left corner of the video; the rows slide when a racer overtakes.
Controls.rcMiniMapTip: The whole track on the right: swap zones, turbo pads, lap lines, the part in view and a dot per racer.
Controls.rcCupTip: Keep a points table across consecutive races in this browser: every race scores F1 points (25-18-15-12-10-8-6-4-2-1) and the table shows after the podium. Restart for the next race.
Controls.rcCupTitleTip: The name on the cup table. Leave it empty to name the cup after the obstacle mix – “Turbo Dash Cup”, “Swap Zone Cup”…
Controls.rcCupEmpty: No races scored yet – finish a race to start the table.
Controls.rcWinnerTip: Stage the result: the director favours this racer – a swap zone never pulls it back, zones it has not reached yet wait for it, turbo pads boost it harder and the last swap zone hands it the lead. Deterministic, so a found seed replays the same win.
Controls.rcWinnerWarning: Staged: this racer is favoured at the swap zones and turbo pads, so the race is rigged.
Controls.rcRigNote: Rigged race: {name} is favoured at the swap zones and turbo pads.
Controls.rcTeamsNote: In the Square Racing Grand Prix the roster names, colours and emoji the first six racers (the others race in colours of their own).
Controls.btDesc: Squares with hit points bounce and clash in the style of project.jdm: the faster square deals the damage, hit squares flash and shrink, and at 0 HP they are knocked out. The last square standing wins – every clash and bounce is a note.
Controls.ctfDesc: Two teams of bouncing squares in the style of project.jdm: touch the enemy flag to carry it and bring it to your base to score. A carrier hit by an enemy drops the flag where it is – every capture plays a goal fanfare.
Controls.btCountTip: How many squares fight, 2–20. Each one is its own team; they are sized automatically to fill the arena (Ball Size makes them bigger).
Controls.btHpTip: The HP every square starts with, 3–20. More HP means longer battles.
Controls.btDamageTip: Damage multiplier: a clash deals this much times the closing speed over the Ball Speed, so a head-on crash hurts far more than a graze.
Controls.btArenaTip: Fight in a box or in a circle, both filling the centre of the video under the scoreboard.
Controls.btShrinkTip: From the eighth second the safe zone closes in over 30 s and pushes the squares together – never tighter than the survivors need.
Controls.btPowerUpsTip: Heal (+35 % HP), shield (blocks the next hit) and speed (1.5× for 5 s) appear at seeded times and places; the square that touches one takes it.
Controls.ctfPerTeamTip: Team size, 1–4 a side (2 – 2 is the classic).
Controls.ctfScoreToWinTip: The first team to bring the enemy flag home this many times wins; otherwise the better score wins when the clip ends.
Controls.ctfTimeInfo: Time limit: {seconds}s (the clip length minus the winner banner)
Controls.arenaNudgeTip: How far the director turns a wall rebound toward the action – the nearest opponent, the enemy flag or home with it. 0 is pure physics; it is seeded, so every run stays reproducible.
Controls.arenaTeamsHint: Names and colours come from the Teams roster when you set one (Teams & Scoreboard section); otherwise every square gets a colour name.
Controls.batchRenderTip: Queue many fast exports: N random seeds or a pasted list of seeds and share links, optionally in every mode or with one setting swept from A to B. The clips render one after another with the settings of this panel (the page shows each one while it renders and gets your settings back at the end), download as mode-seed-duration files and, at the end, all together as a ZIP. The last batch is remembered in this browser.
Controls.batchDownloadEachTip: Saves every clip as soon as it is rendered (the browser may ask once to allow several downloads). Either way, all clips can be downloaded together as a ZIP at the end.
Controls.rrDesc: A square runs along the floor under a scrolling camera; spikes, pits and blocks sit on the beat of the loaded song (or the BPM of the Custom Sound section), so every real-gravity jump lands exactly on a beat and plays the next note.
Controls.rrAutoJumpTip: On: the square jumps by itself at the times the jump solver planned – it never fails and every landing is on the beat. Off: you jump with Space (or ↑ / a tap on the canvas); a crash restarts the section at its checkpoint, and Escape pauses.
Controls.rrObstaclesTip: How many obstacles the course has before the finish line (at the default tempo a run takes about a second and a half per obstacle).
Controls.rrSpeedTip: Horizontal speed of the square in cube lengths per second. Faster makes the jumps longer and the obstacles wider.
Controls.rrJumpTip: How high a jump goes, in cube lengths. With the Gravity of the Ball & Physics section it sets the take-off speed and the flight time the solver times every jump with.
Controls.rrDensityTip: How often an obstacle takes the earliest beat it fits on. Lower leaves a beat or two free now and then (chosen by the seed).
Controls.rrMixTip: What the course is built from: a mix, only rows of spikes, blocks to jump onto and drop off, or pits.
Controls.rrBeatSourceTip: Song: the obstacles follow the detected beat of the loaded song (Background Music or Song Slicer – the detector of Picture Paint), or the BPM while no song is loaded. BPM: always the BPM of the Custom Sound section.
Controls.rrBeatInfoNoSong: No song loaded – following the BPM of the Custom Sound section: {bpm}.
Controls.rrBeatInfoBpm: Following the BPM of the Custom Sound section: {bpm}.
Controls.rrRunInfo: {obstacles} obstacles on a {bpm} BPM beat – a run of about {seconds}s (the seed moves it by a few beats).
Controls.rrManualInfo: {obstacles} obstacles – press Space (or tap the canvas) to jump. A crash restarts the section; Find Simulation needs Auto Jump.
Controls.pdDesc: A ball falls onto a platform that slides left and right. Every catch plays the next note and launches the ball back up – higher from the centre, lower and sideways with spin from the edges – off the walls and the ceiling. Miss too often and it is game over.
Controls.pdAutoTip: On: a deterministic controller predicts every landing and moves the platform there (the Skill slider decides how well). Off: you move it with the pointer or ← → (A / D).
Controls.pdSkillTip: How well the controller plays. Below 100% it plans some catches a little early or late, aims a little off and reacts later – all from the seed, so the misses and the game over come at the same moments every time for a seed. At 100% it never misses.
Controls.pdMissesTip: Misses before the next one ends the game (the hearts above the field).
Controls.pdWidthTip: Width of the platform as a share of the field.
Controls.pdSpinTip: How much a hit off the platform's centre kicks the ball sideways and spins it (the platform's own motion adds a little).
Controls.pdSpeedUpTip: Every catch makes the flight this much faster (up to twice as fast): the longer the game, the harder it gets.
Controls.pdInfoPerfect: At 100% skill the controller never misses – the game never ends (Find Simulation needs a lower skill).
Controls.pdInfoAuto: {lives} lives – the controller's misses come from the seed, so Find Simulation can time the game over.
Controls.pdInfoManual: Move the platform with the pointer or ← →. Find Simulation needs Auto Platform.
Controls.splitIntro: Race 2 or 4 arenas at once on one canvas and in one recording. Every arena plays the settings above; give each one a label and, if you like, its own seed, gravity, ball speed, ball colour or mode.
Controls.splitArenaCountTip: How many arenas race at the same time. 1 is the classic single view; 2 and 4 split the exported square between them.
Controls.splitLayoutTip: Row puts the arenas side by side. Grid makes a 2 × 2 grid of four, or stacks two on top of each other – the better fit for vertical 1080×1920 clips.
Controls.splitSoundTip: Whose bounces you hear: only the first arena's (the cleanest mix), or every arena's (the other arenas a little softer).
Controls.splitArenasTip: Every arena plays the shared settings. Anything you set here replaces them for that one arena only.
Controls.splitArenaModeFirst: The first arena always plays the mode picked above.
Controls.splitArenaSeedTip: A fixed seed replays exactly the same run in this arena on every restart. Leave it empty for a new random run each time. Find Simulation fills the seeds in for you.
Controls.splitRaceNote: A banner shows which arena escaped – or finished – first, and when. Every arena is timed on its own simulation clock, so the race is fair at any frame rate.
Controls.splitFinderNote: Find Simulation searches a seed for every arena (the same target) and stores them above; the clip then lasts until the last arena is done.
Controls.splitFastExportNote: Fast export renders a single arena – record a race with Record Video.
Controls.splitSingleNote: Pick 2 or 4 arenas to start a split-screen race.
Controls.vxDesc: Balls enter at the rim one after another and spiral into the hole under a central pull. Every sound ring a ball sinks past plays the next note of your scale (the Scale and Root note of the sound settings); the hole swallows it with a pew.
Controls.vxBallsTip: How many balls go down the vortex (1–30). Each one plays every ring on its way in, so more balls means denser arpeggios.
Controls.vxStaggerTip: Seconds between two balls entering at the rim. 0 sends them all in at once, spread around the rim; a longer gap turns the notes into a canon.
Controls.vxRingsTip: How many ring lines sit between the rim and the hole (6–24). The ring at the rim plays the lowest note, each ring further in the next note of the scale.
Controls.vxDurationTip: Seconds a ball takes from the rim to the hole. The rings are spaced so it crosses them at a steady tempo; the seed nudges that tempo by up to ±8 %, which is what Find Simulation searches.
Controls.vxGravityTip: How strongly the centre pulls. It sets the whirl – how many laps a ball makes on the way down – not how long the trip takes.
Controls.vxDepthScaleTip: A 3-D feel: balls shrink as they sink toward the hole and the throat of the funnel gets darker. 0 keeps everything flat.
Controls.vxLoopTip: A swallowed ball comes straight back at the rim, so the vortex never ends – great for long loops, but Find Simulation has nothing to time.
Controls.vxRunInfo: {notes} ring notes; the run lasts about {seconds}s (the seed's tempo: {min}–{max}s), so Find Simulation can hit a length in that band.
Controls.vxRunEndless: Respawn Loop is on: the balls come back forever, so the run never ends and Find Simulation is hidden. Switch the loop off to search a seed for your clip length.
Controls.bdDesc: A ball drops and bounces from obstruction to obstruction – every one flies in from off-screen and settles just before its beat, so every landing is exactly on the beat of the song or the BPM.
Controls.bdKindsTip: Which obstructions fly in: planks, blocks, spring pads (a higher bounce with a boing), wedges (they send the ball sideways), spinning bars (flat exactly at the beat) and big drum pads. Keep at least one.
Controls.bdDriftTip: How far the ball drifts sideways from one landing to the next (0 = straight down). Wedges send it sideways whatever this says.
Controls.bdScrollTip: Endless: every landing is a little lower and the camera follows the ball down forever. Arena: the ball bounces around inside the view.
Controls.bdBounceHeightTip: How high a flight of one beat rises, as a share of the view. The gravity follows the tempo, so every tempo bounces this high.
Controls.bdAnticipationTip: How long before its beat an obstruction starts flying in (0.3–1 beats). It always settles a hair before the beat.
Controls.bdSoundTip: Drums: a kick on beats 1 and 3, a snare on 2 and 4, hats on the off-beats, plus each obstruction's own accent. Melody: the next note of the melody (or a built-in tune) on every landing. With background music the song leads and the landings accent it.
Controls.bdColorModeTip: A colour per kind of obstruction, a rainbow that shifts with every beat, or the team roster's colours (the ball wears the first).
Controls.bdTrailTip: A fading trail behind the ball along its arc.
Controls.bdBeatSong: Landing on the loaded song's beat: {bpm} BPM.
Controls.bdBeatBpm: Landing on the BPM setting: {bpm} BPM (load background music to land on a song's beat).
Controls.bdBeatMedia: Landing on the beat of the imported video / audio: {bpm} BPM.
Controls.bdBeatMarkers: Landing on your beat markers: {bpm} BPM.
Controls.bdRunInfo: {beats} landings at {bpm} BPM in the {clip}s clip – the run ends at {seconds}s. It can't miss: every seed lands every beat, so Find Simulation just picks one.
Controls.vbSourceTip: Which beat every rhythm feature follows – the beat lock, On beat, Picture Paint, the Beat Runner: the BPM setting, the loaded song's detected beats, an imported video or audio file, or markers you placed by hand.
Controls.vbMediaTip: Import a video (MP4, WebM, MOV) or an audio file: its sound becomes the background music (so the export carries it) and its beats are detected in your browser. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.
Controls.vbMarkersTip: Your own beat grid on the waveform: click to add or remove a marker, drag one to move it, tap along with T, or start from the detected beats and fix them. Markers travel in links and presets.
Controls.vbVideoBgTip: Draws the imported video, dimmed, behind the arena – in sync with the simulation clock, in recordings and in the fast export.
Controls.vbOnBeatTip: The ring modes time every flight so the ball hits the wall on the beat grid: after each bounce the ball's speed along its path is nudged (never its position), within the On beat range. Short hops that no beat can reach fly free.
Controls.vbOnBeatRangeTip: How much faster or slower On beat may make a flight. Wider lands more hits on the beat, narrower keeps the motion more natural.
Controls.viralBotTip: Plans clips after the playbook of the accounts that go viral (a one-line hook, a countdown, the payoff in the last seconds, alternating endings), scores each one, renders them all with the fast export and downloads a ZIP with the videos, captions, a manifest and a posting schedule.
Controls.journeyDesc: The ball clears one stage after another on its way HOME while the camera scrolls down with it. Build the route below – every stage with its own size – or let the seed draw a random one.
Controls.journeyAutoStagesTip: 0 plays your stage list. 1–12 draws a random journey of that many stages (plus HOME) from the seed, so every seed – and every seed Find Simulation tries – is a new route.
Controls.journeyStagesTip: The route from top to bottom. Pick each stage's size (S, M, L: fewer or more rings, panes, pegs or gates and a taller stage), move it with the arrows, remove it with ✕ or add one before HOME. HOME is always last.
Controls.journeyStagesCodeTip: The route as text: stage names separated by commas, "-s" or "-l" for a small or large stage (e.g. rings,pegs-l,glass-s,multipliers,home). Paste one to load a route – it is what share links carry.
Controls.journeyRunInfo: {count, plural, one {# stage} other {# stages}}, then HOME. Every journey ends at HOME, so Find Simulation can pick a seed for your clip length.
Controls.journeyRunAuto: A random journey of {count, plural, one {# stage} other {# stages}}, then HOME – the seed draws the route, so every seed plays a new one.
Controls.byDesc: Balls are launched from the top one after another, bounce through a short field of pegs and bumpers and land on the target at the bottom: the ring they land in scores (10 for the centre, 0 off the target) and every ball sticks where it lands, so later shots can bounce off earlier ones. Pegs play notes of your scale, landings thud; a centre hit is a BULLSEYE! with confetti, a fanfare and slow motion.
Controls.byShotsTip: How many balls are launched at the target (1–30). The final banner shows the total and the best shot.
Controls.byIntervalTip: Seconds between two launches. Short intervals put several balls in the air at once.
Controls.byChaosTip: How many pegs and bumpers stand between the launcher and the target: 0 is a clear shot, 100% the full field. The seed picks which ones.
Controls.byRingsTip: Scoring rings of the target (3–10). The centre always scores 10 and the outer rings less; fewer rings make each ring wider.
Controls.byTargetMovingTip: The target slides left and right (a little smaller, to have room) and carries the balls stuck in it.
Controls.byPerfectTip: Rigging: the director steers this shot into the bullseye – it bounces through the pegs as usual, then curves onto the centre. Off leaves every shot to the physics.
Controls.byRunInfo: {shots} shots – about {seconds}s with the final banner. The seed decides where every ball lands (and how long the last one bounces), so Find Simulation can hit your clip length.
Controls.byPerfectInfo: Shot {shot} is rigged to hit the bullseye.
Controls.byPerfectBeyond: The perfect shot comes after the last of the {shots} shots, so no shot is rigged.
Controls.bounceMathTip: Rules that change a value by a mathematical step every time something happens – the ball gets bouncier, faster or bigger on every bounce, gravity flips every bar, the ball pumps on the beat. Rules apply in list order, and there is no upper limit unless you set a max.
Controls.bounceMathShowValuesTip: A small badge on the video with the bounciness, speed, size and gravity of the ball that bounced last and how often each rule fired.
Controls.publishTip: Send the finished clip to your TikTok, Instagram and YouTube accounts – several per platform – in one click: YouTube straight from the browser, TikTok and Instagram through a small relay you host, or the no-setup share buttons.
Controls.tyDesc: oddplayground's pong-wars battle: 2 or 4 teams of bouncing balls paint a tile map. A ball passes through its own colour and bounces off any other, converting the tile it hits – so every bounce moves the border. When the countdown runs out, the team with the most tiles wins.
Controls.tyTeamsTip: 2 teams split the board into top and bottom halves, 4 teams into quadrants. Every team starts with the same number of tiles.
Controls.tyRosterNote: The first {count} of {teams} teams wear the Teams & Scoreboard roster; the rest use the neon palette.
Controls.tyPaletteNote: Palette: {names} – or set a roster in Teams & Scoreboard.
Controls.tyBallsPerTeamTip: How many balls every team starts with inside its region (1–8). More balls, faster borders – 4 teams × 8 balls is 32 balls on the board.
Controls.tyPowersTip: One power per team. The HUD calls a team by its power (VORTEX 52% VS BOMBER 48%), or by its name without one.
Controls.tyHintNone: None: classic pong wars – bounce off an enemy tile and convert the tile you hit.
Controls.tyHintVortex: Vortex: the ball's path curves, and on every power tick it drags a whirl whose two spiral arms convert the enemy tiles within the reach.
Controls.tyHintBomber: Bomber: on every power tick the ball arms and blows on its next bounce off an enemy tile – every tile within the reach turns its colour, nearby balls are blown away and the board shakes. One bounce can flip the board.
Controls.tyHintPainter: Painter: on every power tick the ball dashes straight through enemy territory, painting a one-tile trail.
Controls.tyHintGhost: Ghost: a fast, weightless ball that passes through enemy tiles without bouncing and converts the 3×3 block it is in on every wall bounce.
Controls.tyPowerEveryTip: Seconds between two ticks of a timed power (the vortex's whirl, the bomber's blast, the painter's dash). Every ball starts its timer at a seeded offset, so a team's balls do not fire together.
Controls.tyRadiusTip: How far the vortex's whirl and the bomber's blast reach, in tiles.
Controls.tyColsTip: Tiles across the board (12–48); the rows follow the board's shape. More tiles, finer borders – the balls shrink with the tiles.
Controls.tyDurationTip: When the countdown runs out the team with the most tiles wins (a level top is a draw). The recording length follows it, plus a few seconds for the verdict. The last 5 seconds get intense: the balls speed up.
Controls.tyPegsTip: The faint dotted grid of the reels: a dot every three tiles, and the dots deflect the balls.
Controls.tyBadgeTip: The "FLASHING LIGHTS – THE END GETS INTENSE" badge in the top-left corner of the clip.
Controls.tyHudTip: The band over the board: PICK A SIDE, the countdown, the VS line with every team's share and the live percentage bar. With a team roster it also stands in for the scoreboard.
Controls.mzDesc: oddplayground's maze reels: a seeded perfect maze with a red entrance slot on top and an exit gap at the bottom. The balls drop in one after another, bounce their way through and paint every cell they pass – the first one out wins, and the notes climb as they near the exit.
Controls.mzBrainTip: How the balls find their way. Bounce: pure physics – they just ricochet through the corridors. Wall follower: one hand on the wall at every junction – it always finds the exit. Explorer: prefers the corridors it has not been down yet and backtracks from dead ends. The steering nudges a ball as it crosses the centre of a cell.
Controls.mzHintBounce: Pure physics: the balls ricochet through the corridors and may take a long time to find the exit.
Controls.mzHintWallFollow: Keeps a hand on the wall at every junction – slow but sure: it always gets out.
Controls.mzHintExplorer: Prefers the corridors it has not visited yet and backtracks from dead ends (a depth-first search).
Controls.mzHandTip: Which hand the wall follower keeps on the wall. Alternate gives the balls different hands, so a race takes different routes.
Controls.mzBallsTip: How many balls race through the maze, 1–8. They drop in through the entrance a moment apart and fly through each other. A roster in Teams & Scoreboard gives the first ones (up to six) its colours and names.
Controls.mzRosterNote: The first {count} of {balls} balls wear the Teams & Scoreboard roster; the rest use the neon palette.
Controls.mzPaletteNote: Palette: {names} – or set a roster in Teams & Scoreboard.
Controls.mzColsTip: Columns of the maze, 6–40; the rows follow from the portrait shape. A bigger maze has narrower corridors (the balls shrink to fit) and takes longer to solve.
Controls.mzSpeedTip: How fast the balls travel, relative to the maze's width (the Ball Speed slider does not apply here).
Controls.mzGravityTip: A downward pull, 0–1: the balls fall down the vertical corridors and have to climb back up (the steering gives a ball the speed to climb one cell).
Controls.mzTrailTip: Every cell a ball visits is painted, so the maze slowly fills with “blood”. This sets the paint's opacity; 0 turns it off.
Controls.mzTrailOwnTip: Each ball paints its corridors in its own colour instead of the trail colour.
Controls.mzTrailColorTip: The colour of the painted corridors (blood red by default).
Controls.mzFogTip: Hides the cells no ball has visited yet, except for a clear circle around every ball – for suspense. 0 turns it off.
Controls.mzWallColorTip: The colour of the glowing maze walls.
Controls.mzDurationTip: The run ends when every ball is out, or after this many seconds – if nobody got out by then, the ball nearest the exit wins.
Controls.mzBadgeTip: The “FLASHING LIGHTS – THE END GETS INTENSE” badge in the top-left corner of the clip.
Controls.mzHudTip: A row per ball in the top-right corner: its colour, its name and a bar that fills as it gets closer to the exit, with the passages left to go (or its place once it is out).
Controls.mzRunInfo: A {cols} × {rows} maze ({cells} cells, a new one for every seed); the run ends when every ball is out, at {seconds}s at the latest.
Controls.cvDesc: A belt across the top carries a ball out of the hatch every few seconds and drops it into the arena below. In the rings every ball has to escape on its own (the rings never break, and the director helps a ball that has been stuck for a while); the escaped balls ride the bottom belt out of the field. The bowl fills up and spills over; the peg field sorts the balls into bins. The belt hums while it carries a ball and clicks when one drops, and every bounce plays a note of your scale.
Controls.cvArenaTip: What the balls drop into: concentric rings with rotating gaps (the Wall Count, Gap Size and Rotation of the wall settings apply), a bowl that piles them up, or a peg field over bins.
Controls.cvHintRings: Each ball slides down a tube into the core and has to find the gaps to get out. Escapes are counted, and the bottom belt carries the escaped balls away.
Controls.cvHintBowl: The balls pile up in a bowl and settle – about 30 balls (at the chosen Ball Size) fit before the first one rolls over the rim; whatever spills falls onto the bottom belt and counts as overflow.
Controls.cvHintPegs: The balls bounce through a field of pegs – every peg a note, low on the left, high on the right – and pile up in the bins below.
Controls.cvIntervalTip: Seconds between two balls on the belt: a ball comes out of the hatch every interval and drops off the belt's end about a second later.
Controls.cvMaxBallsTip: How many balls the belt loads (1–200). The run ends once the last one is out of the rings or the arena has settled.
Controls.cvFreezeTip: A ball that lands freezes in place and becomes an obstacle, so the pile grows visibly (Accumulation style). In the rings a ball's freedom lasts four seconds, then it freezes where it is.
Controls.cvVarietyTip: How much the balls' sizes and colours vary: 0 sends Gerald's identical twins down the belt, 100% a mix of sizes and colours. The first ball is always Gerald.
Controls.cvRunInfo: {balls, plural, one {# ball} other {# balls}} – about {seconds}s with the final banner. The seed decides every bounce (and how long the last ball takes), so Find Simulation can hit your clip length.
Controls.respawnEveryTip: A new ball drops in from the top every this many seconds (0 = off). In Classic it stops once every ring is broken.
Controls.exitBehaviorTip: How every ring’s exit moves. Rotate: it turns with its ring, as always. Jump: it teleports to another spot of the ring every few seconds, or as soon as the ball gets close. Flee: it runs away from the ball along the ring. Shrink: it narrows until it shuts, then opens again somewhere else. Deterministic: seeds, links and Find Simulation include it.
Controls.exitRotateDesc: The exits turn with their rings, as always.
Controls.exitJumpDesc: Every exit teleports to a new spot of its ring on a timer – and jumps away when the ball comes within its sense. A flash marks where it was and where it lands.
Controls.exitFleeDesc: The exit runs away from the ball along its ring while the ball is within its sense. To get out, the ball has to out-run it.
Controls.exitShrinkDesc: The exit narrows over the exit timer until it shuts, then opens again somewhere else.
Controls.exitHoldNote: The rings hold still: the exits move by themselves.
Controls.exitJumpSecondsTip: Jump: seconds between two jumps. Shrink: seconds an exit takes to close (1–10 on the slider; type any longer time).
Controls.exitSenseTip: How close the ball may come to an exit – in degrees round the ring – before it reacts: a jumping exit flickers and jumps away (a ball that gets there first escapes), a fleeing one starts to run. 0 = it never reacts.
Controls.exitFleeSpeedTip: Top speed of a fleeing exit along its ring, in degrees a second. The ball has to move round the ring faster than that to catch it.
Controls.splatBarrierTip: Every wall hit leaves a splat of paint in the ball’s colour on the inside of the wall – and the splats are solid, so the ball slowly builds its own barrier.
